prestol.guide.army.1: MineColonies guard towers and barracks towers keep a garrison of Hundred Years War soldiers instead of guards: %s per building level. Warriors, spearmen, shieldmen, archers or crossbowmen are chosen on the Army page.
prestol.guide.army.2: A soldier is one of your citizens: an idle citizen takes up arms and moves to the tower, and when the garrison is dismissed he comes home with his name and skills. A fallen soldier is a dead citizen.
prestol.guide.army.3: A recruit needs a weapon (sword, spear, shield, bow or crossbow with arrows) and food, taken from the tower itself, the warehouse or the town hall. A new soldier comes every %s s until the garrison is full; no recruits come during a siege.
prestol.guide.army.4: The archery trains marksmen and the combat academy trains the foot: +1 rank every %s min. The garrison's task (guard, patrol, follow a player) is set in the tower window, Settings tab.
prestol.guide.army.5: There are no Hundred Years War workers here: MineColonies citizens do their work.
prestol.guide.banner.1: A realm has a colour and a coat of arms taken from its MineColonies colony flag. A realm standard costs %s wool and a stick and is handed out on the Banner page. The realm's flag flies over every town hall and Hundred Years War armies carry it.
prestol.guide.banner.2: You can draw your own flag: Banner → "Draw your own flag…". There are a brush, a fill, a picker, paints and any colour of your own, undo (Ctrl+Z) and mirror. The ruler draws and raises the flag.
prestol.guide.banner.3: A ready picture can be loaded from a link (png, jpg, gif) or simply dropped as a file onto the editor; touch it up before raising it.
prestol.guide.decrees.1: A decree is a temporary measure for one settlement: a festival, a great building, mobilisation, a harvest decree and more. After a decree you must wait before issuing it again. In the capital decrees are %s%% stronger.
prestol.guide.decrees.2: A law holds in the whole realm until it is repealed. The number of laws depends on the realm's rank; after a repeal a new law can only be enacted after %s min.
prestol.guide.drinks.1: With Let's Do Brewery and Vinery a colony gets a brewer's hut and a winemaker's hut. Place them with the build tool: packs "Prestol: Brewery" and "Prestol: Winery".
prestol.guide.drinks.2: The hut block is crafted like a MineColonies hut: planks around, the golden sceptre on top and a wooden brewing station (brewer) or a fermentation barrel (winemaker) in the middle.
prestol.guide.drinks.3: The brewer dries grain and brews beer and whiskey; the winemaker presses grapes and apples and makes wines and ciders. He orders hops, barley, grapes, bottles and water buckets through the warehouse. The finest drinks open at hut levels 2 and 3.
prestol.guide.founded: "%s" is founded: this is your hamlet. Grow it into a village and a town, then found a realm. The Realm Book (%s) tells how in its Guide.
prestol.guide.lands.1: A realm takes land by chunks on the Xaero world map: hold the right mouse button, drag a rectangle and choose "Prestol: take land". Only unclaimed land next to your own, within %s chunks of a town hall, can be taken.
prestol.guide.lands.2: Land limit: %1$s chunks per settlement, %2$s per town hall level and %3$s per building. The realm's lands are painted in its colour on the map, and its banner flies over its settlements.
prestol.guide.militia.1: When a town hall is besieged, its people take up arms: a militia gathers at the town hall, one man per %s adult citizens, more in villages, towns and the capital. A militiaman is a citizen: the fallen do not come back.
prestol.guide.militia.2: The town hall window has a "Hire mercenaries" button: the squad takes %1$s gold ingots per man, follows the hirer and serves for %2$s min. Mercenaries bring their own bread.
prestol.guide.provisions.1: Every soldier carries provisions, 0 to 100%%. A full stock lasts %s game days. Soldiers do not need Hundred Years War supply: they eat ordinary food.
prestol.guide.provisions.2: Below 60%% a soldier refills on his own: from his tower, from the warehouse and town hall of his owner's or his realm's settlement, from Hundred Years War supply points, or from his commander's pack when he is near.
prestol.guide.provisions.3: A hungry soldier weakens, a starving one also slows down, and after %s game days of hunger he deserts: a drafted citizen goes home. Look at your soldier to see his rank and provisions over the hotbar.
prestol.guide.realm.1: A settlement owner founds a realm on the Realm page: give it a name and the settlement becomes its capital. A proper capital is a town with at least %s citizens: only such a town can be made the capital later, and the more citizens it has, the more settlements the realm can take.
prestol.guide.realm.2: A realm may hold %1$s settlements and one more for every %2$s citizens of its capital. The ruler invites free settlements on the Settlements page, and owners may ask to join. Settlements stay with their owners.
prestol.guide.realm.3: A realm rises in rank: Principality → Kingdom (%1$s subjects and %2$s towns) → Empire (%3$s subjects and %4$s towns).
prestol.guide.realm.4: The ruler decides on war and peace, moves the capital and enacts laws. During a war the realm cannot be disbanded and the capital cannot be moved.
prestol.guide.settlements.1: Every MineColonies colony is a settlement. A hamlet is any settlement. A village needs %1$s citizens, a level %2$s town hall and %3$s buildings; a town %4$s citizens, a level %5$s town hall and %6$s buildings. Only finished buildings count.
prestol.guide.settlements.2: If citizens or buildings are lost, a settlement declines and loses its tier. The higher the tier, the larger its militia and mercenary squads. The Settlements page shows what the next tier needs.
prestol.guide.settlements.3: Mind the happiness: below %1$s of 10 for %2$s days in a row, a settlement mutinies and leaves the realm.
prestol.guide.start.1: Prestol joins MineColonies colonies into realms. Everything is run from this book; it opens with %s. The pages are the ribbons on the right; hover a button or a line to see a hint.
prestol.guide.start.2: 1. Place a MineColonies town hall: this is your hamlet.
prestol.guide.start.3: 2. Build houses and workshops and bring in citizens: the hamlet grows into a village, then a town.
prestol.guide.start.4: 3. Found a realm on the Realm page: your settlement becomes its capital.
prestol.guide.start.5: 4. Invite other owners, take land, issue decrees, keep garrisons in your towers.
prestol.guide.start.6: 5. Once the realm is strong, make alliances, declare wars and take enemy settlements.
prestol.guide.war.1: The ruler declares war on the War and Peace page. The troops muster for %s min; no siege can start before that. Enemy players become Hostile in your settlements and the guards attack them.
prestol.guide.war.2: To take a settlement, stand by the enemy town hall (within %1$s blocks) and hold it for %2$s min. While a defender is alive nearby (a soldier, a militiaman or a player) the time stands still. If all attackers leave, the siege is lifted.
prestol.guide.war.3: A siege can only start while the settlement's owner or an officer is online.
prestol.guide.war.4: The capital falls last: it can only be besieged when the realm has no other settlements.
prestol.guide.war.5: The victor decides the settlement's fate: keep it, sack it (the loot chests by the town hall open only for the victors for %1$s min) or enslave its people (%2$s%% of the slaves die at each dawn). A taken settlement cannot be taken again for %3$s game days.
prestol.guide.war.6: Peace needs the consent of both sides and is followed by a truce of %s game days.
prestol.guide.war.7: The former owner of a taken settlement may raise a revolution after %1$s game days if its happiness is below %2$s: he must hold the town hall for %3$s min.
prestol.guide.war.8: A Hundred Years War captain gives orders within 512 blocks and loaded land. The war elephant walks over uneven ground and breaks through leaves.
prestol.guide.welcome: Welcome! Realms rule here: settlements grow, realms go to war and armies are raised from citizens. Press %s to open the Realm Book and read its Guide.
